title: <script setup> & Reactivity
body:
# `<script setup>` & Reactivity

## The modern SFC

```html
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'

const count = ref(0)
const doubled = computed(() => count.value * 2)
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="count++">{{ count }} → {{ doubled }}</button>
</template>
```

Top-level bindings are exposed to the template automatically — no `export
default`, no Options API ceremony.

## Choosing the right primitive

| Primitive | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `ref(v)` | Single values; `.value` in JS, unwrapped in template |
| `reactive(obj)` | Object/grouped state; no reassignment of the proxy itself |
| `computed(fn)` | Derived values — cached until dependencies change |
| `watch(src, cb)` | Side effects on change (persistence, analytics-free logging) |

```ts
const state = reactive({ items: [] as string[] })
state.items.push('x')            // fine
// state = reactive(...)         // ❌ loses reactivity — use ref instead
```

## One-way data flow

Data flows **down** via props; events flow **up** via emits. Two children never
talk directly — they coordinate through their parent or a store.

`watch` is for side effects only; when you can compute it, prefer `computed`
(no stale-state bugs, auto-tracked deps).

examples.name: Counter.vue

exercise.prompt: Build a temperature converter component: Celsius input drives a computed Fahrenheit readout (F = C × 9/5 + 32), rounded to 1 decimal.
exercise.starterCode:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
const celsius = ref(20)
// TODO: fahrenheit computed
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model.number="celsius" aria-label="Celsius" />
  <output>{{ fahrenheit }} °F</output>
</template>
hints: Round via Math.round(x*10)/10 for one decimal.
exercise.solution:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
const celsius = ref(20)
const fahrenheit = computed(() => Math.round((celsius.value * 9) / 5 + 32))
</script>

<template>
  <input v-model.number="celsius" aria-label="Celsius" />
  <output>{{ fahrenheit }} °F</output>
</template>
